title: Augmentation-compatible base change for two ordered localization models
statement: Let $\varphi:A\to B$ be a homomorphism of commutative rings and let $I\subset A$, $J\subset B$ be finitely generated ideals with $\varphi(I)B=J$. Let $(P,\epsilon_P:P\to A[0])$ and $(L,\epsilon_L:L\to B[0])$ be augmented integer cochain complexes of module sheaves on the one-object bottom sites. Assume the ordinary derived categories [def-weil-abstract-derived-category], the augmented ordered localization-model properties $\operatorname{RingComplexHasCechModel}(A,I,P,\epsilon_P)$ and $\operatorname{RingComplexHasCechModel}(B,J,L,\epsilon_L)$ of [def-weil-pbc-ring-complex-cech-data], and acyclic-tensor K-flatness of $P$ [def-pc-kflat-complex]. Let $E_\varphi P$ be the actual termwise scalar extension of [def-weil-pbc-ring-complex-semilinear-extension]. If $\chi:E_\varphi P\to L$ is a cochain map such that $\epsilon_L(\chi(1\otimes x))=\varphi(\epsilon_P(x))$ for every degree-zero section $x$ of $P$, where $1\otimes x$ is sent into the sheafification by its actual unit, then $\chi$ is a quasi-isomorphism. Only these two complexes and this single augmentation equation are assumed; no functorial family occurs.

proof.text: Choose a finite list generating I. The ordered localization complex is bounded because there are no increasing tuples longer than the list. Each term is flat: finite products equal finite direct sums and localization is flat. Thus it is K-flat. Use the two augmented derived model isomorphisms. Since P is K-flat, its ordinary scalar extension computes its derived extension. More explicitly, represent the augmented derived model isomorphism by a common cochain roof. Replace its source by a K-flat resolution. Both composite legs are quasi-isomorphisms between K-flat complexes, so changeOfRings_kFlat_quasiIso preserves them for the actual additive scalar-extension functor; its object and map equations are definitional. Inverting these legs gives the derived extension comparison, including its augmentation equation.

For each product g of generators the isomorphism B tensor_A A[1/g] to B[1/phi(g)] sends b tensor a/g^n to b phi(a)/phi(g)^n; the inverse sends b/phi(g)^n to b tensor 1/g^n. Tensor balancing and the localization relations verify the inverses even when phi(g)=0. The isomorphisms commute with the localization face maps and augmentations, yielding an augmented cochain isomorphism E(C_A(f)) to C_B(phi(f)).

For C_B, composition with C_B to B[0] is a bijection Hom(T,C_B) to Hom(T,B[0]) for every derived complex T which becomes zero after localization at each image generator. Indeed the cone is a finite iterated extension of shifts of localization modules. By the extension/restriction adjunction, all shifted Hom groups from T into each of these modules vanish: the localization of T is zero and localization is flat. The finite triangle exact sequences then give bijectivity. Inverting one generator contracts C_B by inserting/deleting that index with its ordered sign; hence E(P), which is isomorphic to E(C_A), satisfies this support condition. The augmentation equation in the statement is equality of the two actual augmented cochain maps by linearity on pure tensors. Under the augmented derived comparisons it therefore identifies chi with the isomorphism in the previous step, by bijectivity. Consequently chi is a quasi-isomorphism. For an empty list C=A[0], and a zero denominator gives the zero localization, so all edge cases obey the same argument.

theorem ringComplex_cech_baseChange_quasiIso
    (A B : CommRingCat.{u}) [HasDerivedCategory.{w} (RingSiteModules A)]
    [HasDerivedCategory.{w} (RingSiteModules B)] (φ : A →+* B)
    (I : {I : Ideal A // I.FG}) (J : {J : Ideal B // J.FG})
    (h : I.val.map φ = J.val)
    (P : CochainComplex (RingSiteModules A) ℤ)
    (L : CochainComplex (RingSiteModules B) ℤ)
    (εP : P ⟶ ringComplexSingle A) (εL : L ⟶ ringComplexSingle B)
    (hCA : RingComplexHasCechModel A I.val P εP)
    (hCB : RingComplexHasCechModel B J.val L εL)
    (hP : P.IsAcyclicTensorKFlat) (χ : ringComplexExtensionComplex φ P ⟶ L)
    (hε : ∀ x : (P.X 0).val.obj (op ⟨PUnit.unit⟩),
      ringComplexAugmentationValue εL
          ((χ.f 0).val.app (op ⟨PUnit.unit⟩)
            ((toSheafify ⊥ (SheafOfModules.changeOfRingsPresheaf
              (ringSiteMap φ) (P.X 0)).presheaf).app (op ⟨PUnit.unit⟩)
                ((1 : B) ⊗ₜ[A, φ] x))) = φ (ringComplexAugmentationValue εP x)) :
    QuasiIso χ
